page.layout: One column of running text with Greek and Latin, and a short dialogue in verse-like lines. No marginal notes. A small black mark at the lower right is not text and is left out.

main_text.p: visa ea vox Græcæ vim non satis explere. Nam ἄνοια omnis, vaecordia est: quippe homo ἄνους caret corde, id est sapientia: unde sunt excors & vaecors, at ἀπόνοια aliud longè est. neque profectò sicut dixit Cicero in Pisonem, ô vaecors & amens: ita dixeris Græcè satis proprie ὦ ἀπονενοημένε ἢ ἀνόητε. Homo ἀπονενοημένος, quem desperatè malum possis Latinè dicere, Ciceroni est homo perditus, vel perditus & profligatus: aut etiam desperatus: ut cum desperatorum hominum flagitiosos græges dixit in Catilina: & alibi sæpe. Nam etsi proprie vox desperatus aliud sonat, tamen de eodem vsurpatur.

Οἱ ὀμόσαι ἐχύ.] Rectissimè prima nota hominis perditi profligatíque hæc ponitur: hic siquidem è numero eorum est, qui ut dixit olim Pacvvius iusiurandum aliud nihil esse censent quàm mantile, quæ noxæ quotidianæ extergeantur. Talis apud Græcum comicum Strepsiades, quem ita alloquitur suus creditor in Nebulis,

Καὶ προσκαθεδεῖλω γ' ὥστ' ὀμόσαι τρισ[?]
Ca. Iurastin' te illam nulli venditurum nisi mihi?
Ba. Fateor. Ca. nempe conceptis verbis. Ba. etiam confultis quoque.

Ca. Periurasti scelefte. Ba. at argentū intra condidi. Athenis qui facile iusiurandū suscipiebant, Ardetti vulgò à loco ubi iurare moris erat, appellabantur, Hesychius. Τοὺς ῥᾳδίως ὀμνύντας ... τοὺς ὅρκους ἰσχὺς ἀρδήττους ἐκάλουν. τότε δ' ὁ ἐν τῷ Ἰλισσῷ, ἰσχὺς Παναθη-ναϊκῶ [?]

page.notes: Greek passages (Hesychius, Aristophanes' Nebulae, the Ἀπονενοημένος entry) are transcribed from the scan and not checked against an edition; several accents and letters are uncertain and should be verified. The line "Δα. Καὶ ταῦτ'" and the Ba./Ca. speaker lines are uncertain in their Greek and Latin letters. "Pacuuius" is kept as Pacvvius per the u/v rule. Printed "confultis" and "scelefte" are kept as printed. The opening Greek word of the paragraph "Οἱ ὀμόσαι" and the final Greek word "Παναθηναϊκῶ" are partly illegible. The line "Athenis qui facile..." may begin a new paragraph; here it is kept joined to the preceding speech because it runs on from a full line without an indent.
